title: اسمه راتب  (Taster: it's called a salary)

segments.t: This is a short Arabic taster from Al Maktab, the Saudi office comedy set in a courier company. Malik, the manager, talks about his staff needing monthly money, and a colleague corrects his choice of word. Listen to four short lines in everyday Saudi Arabic first; you can follow the meaning afterwards.
يعني قصدي.
يحتاجون مصروف شهري.
اسمه راتب.
أنا مسؤول عن كل الناس اللي برا.
Let's take those lines one at a time.
يعني قصدي.

'I mean.' He is correcting himself. The second word literally means 'my intention', with a possessive ending that makes it his own intention. Here the whole phrase simply introduces what he meant to say.
يحتاجون مصروف شهري.
'They need a monthly allowance.' The ending tells us that several people need something. The word meaning 'monthly' comes after the allowance it describes. It is built from the word for 'month'.
اسمه راتب.

'It's called a salary.' Literally, 'its name is a salary'. The word for 'name' has a little ending that points back to the allowance. Her correction is pointed: these are employees' wages, rather than pocket money.
أنا مسؤول عن كل الناس اللي برا.

'I'm responsible for all the people outside.' Arabic places the first-person pronoun directly before the adjective meaning 'responsible'. This present statement needs no separate helping verb. The short linking word introduces a description of those people. Here, 'outside' means beyond the meeting room. Now listen to the same exchange again.
يعني قصدي.
يحتاجون مصروف شهري.
اسمه راتب.
أنا مسؤول عن كل الناس اللي برا.
You heard the difference between an allowance and a salary, and a way to say who you are responsible for. We'll leave Malik with his colleague's useful correction. See you next time.
اسمه راتب.

source.show: Al Maktab (Saudi, 2022), S1E1: four selected lines from the official MBC Shahid clip

lines.fragment: أنا مسؤول عن كل الناس اللي برا
